messages:
jamie (AE): Olivia from BankCo asked if we can provide a fixed list of egress IPs for EU-hosted tenants so they can whitelist at their perimeter. also they want confirmation that inference traffic never leaves eu when 'region: hard_pin' is set.
ashok (SE): we can provide per-region CIDR blocks for known NAT egress endpoints. two caveats: 1) hosted autoscaling may add ephemeral egress addresses, 2) some third-party subprocessors (analytics, monitoring) may contact non-eu endpoints unless disabled.
ashok (SE): sample CIDRs (illustrative):
```
- eu-west-1: 34.120.0.0/18, 35.196.0.0/20
- eu-central-1: 35.156.0.0/19, 34.200.0.0/21
```
jamie (AE): can we commit to those exact blocks? customer needs static allowlist for production.
sara (Infra PM): for Dedicated or Private we can guarantee fixed NAT egress IP(s) per VPC. for Hosted, we provide a conservative published CIDR set that we update with notice; we also offer an option to route tenant egress through a managed NAT with static IPs for an infra add-on (extra cost).
sara (Infra PM): hosted allowlist model: we publish a per-region CIDR bundle and a webhook for change-notifications. recommended for production whitelisting: use Dedicated/Private for strict IP invariance.
kyle (Security): on the data residency point: with routing policy 'hard_pin' and data-plane pinned to EU, model inputs/outputs, KV cache, and storage remain in-region. control-plane telemetry (control APIs, state, heartbeats) may transit to our global control plane unless customer selects Private. we must reflect this in the DPA.
jamie (AE): Olivia, do you need control-plane traffic pinned too or just inference data and logs?
olivia (Customer): want inference data + logs never to leave EU. control-plane metadata is acceptable if it contains no PII, but please confirm we can disable request-level telemetry. also asking for SOC2 attestation and whether we can get a signed copy.
kyle (Security): we can disable request-level telemetry for that tenant and scrub logs. SOC2 report: we provide a signed SOC2 Type II artifact via our compliance portal after a minimal NDA. ISO snippets available too.
legal-bot: note: DPA v3.2 supports a checkbox for private control plane + subprocessor disclosure. can trigger a redline for control-plane residency wording if customer requires.
nashok (SE): ops implication: if a model isn't replicated to EU we return 412 or configurable error when hard_pin is set. we can replicate any supported model on request; estimate: 24-72h for replication + validation depending on model size. one-time replication cost ~ storage_size * storage_unit_cost + transfer/ops (~0.2-0.5 USD/GiB as ballpark).
jamie (AE): need concrete pricing vs timeline for demo vs prod. also customer wants a short runbook for their security team describing the whitelist process.
sara (Infra PM): action: i'll prepare: 1) per-region CIDR bundle (canonical list), 2) Dedicated NAT option pricing, 3) replication cost table by common model sizes. target: EOD PT.
kyle (Security): action: I'll draft a 3-paragraph security note: telemetry disable steps, log redaction, key management options (hosted-managed CMK vs customer KMS via Private), and where SOC2 can be obtained.
nashok (SE): action: i'll make a 1-page POC playbook (how to validate egress, sample curl tests, expected headers, and failure modes). include the sample curl test: `curl -v https://inference.eu.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" --data '{"input":"test"}'` and note the response code when model unavailable under hard_pin.
jamie (AE): olivia, can you confirm urgency: they need these docs for procurement by end of week. also asked if we can provide a signed SOC2 within 48h.
olivia (Customer): procurement deadline is Friday EOD CET. SOC2 in 48h would be ideal.
kyle (Security): we'll surface the signed SOC2 ASAP; availability depends on NDA turnaround but expect portal link within 24-48h after legal clears.
jamie (AE): schedule quick sync: tomor 10:30 CET for 20m?
olivia (Customer): yes, booked.
sara (Infra PM): note: for Hosted whitelists we recommend a layered approach: 1) initial allowlist with published CIDRs 2) test POC using sample IPs 3) move to Dedicated/Private for prod. I'll include a sample CIDR test plan.
deploy-bot: automated: added egress-cidr-publish job to infra-docs; next update scheduled in 12h.
jamie (AE): thanks team. i'll compile and send to BankCo.
(THREAD END)
